title: WIT Studio Teases New Attack on Titan Project: What Could It Be?
summary:
Just when you thought the Titans were gone for good, WIT Studio has stirred the pot. The animation studio responsible for the first 59 episodes of Attack on Titan posted a cryptic teaser on social media, announcing that a new project related to the franchise will be revealed on August 20. The message reads: "It seems that they, during 'that period,' will be holding a special dinner." The accompanying image, drawn by manga author Hajime Isayama, shows Eren, Armin, Mikasa, Levi, Hange, and Erwin—all characters who met tragic fates by the series' end.

The announcement is surprising for several reasons. First, the anime already fully adapted Isayama's manga, concluding in 2023 with a two-part finale and a compilation film titled The Last Attack. There's no obvious source material left to adapt. Second, WIT Studio hasn't been the primary animation studio for the series since 2019, when MAPPA took over for the Final Season. Since then, WIT has focused on hits like Spy x Family and Ranking of Kings.

So why is WIT making this announcement? Last year, Attack on Titan producer Tetsuya Kinoshita said the team planned to continue creating films, concerts, and game collaborations. The upcoming video game Attack on Titan 3 is due out Dec. 10, but no new anime has been officially announced. The teaser's reference to a "special dinner" likely nods to the series' dark themes of cannibalism, while "that period" could hint at a prequel set before the events of the Final Season, when all six characters were still alive. If the image is any clue, we might be getting a story from the Survey Corps' earlier days.

Whatever it is, fans won't have to wait long. The reveal is set for next Thursday, Aug. 20. Until then, the final battle may be about to begin again.
why_it_matters: The announcement shows how successful franchises can extend their lives through prequels, films, and games after the main story ends, which shapes what media gets made. It also raises creative questions about whether returning to characters with known tragic endings adds depth or risks cheapening their original arc.

background_read: Attack on Titan began as a manga by Hajime Isayama (the Japanese comics creator who wrote and drew the full story) and grew into one of the most-watched anime franchises globally.

WIT Studio (the Japanese animation company that produced the first 59 episodes) handed the main animation duties to MAPPA (another Japanese studio) in 2019, which then completed the Final Season in 2023.
The story is set in a walled world where humanity fights giant humanoid Titans, and the Survey Corps is the branch that ventures beyond the walls to learn the truth.

Because the anime already fully adapted the manga, a new project would likely be an original side story, film, concert, game tie-in, or prequel—strategies studios use to keep a franchise alive after the source material ends.
The teaser's 'special dinner' line points toward the series' dark themes of survival and sacrifice, and the image of characters who died makes a prequel setting feel more plausible.

perspectives.description: Fans are excited to see more of the characters and world they love, especially after the anime ended. A prequel could explore unanswered mysteries from the Survey Corps' early days and bring original art by Hajime Isayama back into the spotlight.

Some worry that new projects might milk a finished franchise and undermine the emotional finality of the original ending. If a prequel contradicts established lore or overexplains things, it could feel like a cash grab.

Using an established franchise is lower financial risk for studios than launching an original anime. The shift from WIT to MAPPA also shows how animation production can move between companies while the publisher still commissions new tie-ins.

The Aug. 20 reveal will show whether the franchise is moving toward film, games, or a true anime prequel. A successful project could introduce the series to a new generation of viewers, while a weak one could show the limits of post-ending expansion.
